name: Ademetionine (S-Adenosyl-L-Methionine)
sections: 398.44 g/mol (cation); used as stable salts (1,4-butanedisulfonate or tosylate)
White to off-white hygroscopic powder (salt forms).

A 2020 review found efficacy versus placebo in depression comparable to imipramine/escitalopram, though a 2016 Cochrane review found an absence of high-quality evidence. First approval/introduction: Discovered 1952 (Giulio Cantoni); prescription drug in Italy 1979, Spain 1985, Germany 1989 (Abbott/Knoll); US dietary supplement since 1999.

Physiological methyl donor and precursor of glutathione (via transsulphuration); restores hepatocyte membrane fluidity, improves bile flow and antioxidant capacity in intrahepatic cholestasis and alcoholic/drug-induced liver injury. Also involved in neurotransmitter synthesis (antidepressant effect). Receptor / target profile: Universal methyl donor and precursor of glutathione; restores hepatocyte membrane function and bile flow in cholestasis.
Methyl donation (to S-adenosylhomocysteine), transsulfuration (to cysteine/glutathione) and aminopropylation (polyamines)
Summary: Oral bioavailability low (~5%); Tmax 3–5 h (enteric-coated). Half-life ~1.5 h. Metabolised via methylation and transsulphuration pathways.
Intrahepatic cholestasis in pre-cirrhotic and cirrhotic states
Cholestasis: 800–1600 mg/day in divided doses (oral maintenance after IV initiation)
Take between meals on an empty stomach; swallow whole
Dose to be individualised by the treating physician according to clinical response and tolerability.
Use only if clearly needed (used in cholestasis of pregnancy).
Genetic defects of the methionine cycle (cystathionine beta-synthase deficiency, homocystinuria)
B12/folate deficiency – correct first (may reduce efficacy)
Take on an empty stomach; swallow whole
SSRIs, TCAs, clomipramine, tramadol, tryptophan – risk of serotonin syndrome
Between meals; swallow whole; protect from moisture.
Frezza et al., 1990 – improved pruritus and biochemical cholestasis.
Mato et al., J Hepatol 1999 – trend to improved survival in alcoholic cirrhosis (Child A/B).
Store below 30°C in a dry place, protected from light and moisture. Keep out of the reach of children. Do not use after the expiry date.
